rounds.text: Integra Engineering India Ltd trades at a steep price-to-earnings ratio of 40.2x and a price-to-book multiple of 5.36x [E1, E2]. These valuations represent a severe premium over sector benchmarks, where the sector P/E sits at 26.01x and the sector P/B stands at 2.38x [E6, E7]. This aggressive pricing is entirely disconnected from the company’s recent performance, as compounded sales growth over the trailing twelve months has contracted by -5% and year-over-year sales are down by 3% [E17, E69]. Furthermore, the business offers a dividend yield of 0.00%, failing to reward shareholders while they absorb these elevated valuation multiples [E4]. Growth has also decelerated significantly over shorter horizons, dropping from 10-year and 5-year compounded rates of 20% and 22% down to just 8% over the last 3 years [E14, E15, E16]. Conceded: the company boasts a strong return on assets of 9.77% compared to the sector benchmark of 1.33%, alongside accelerating earnings growth and recent quarter-over-quarter sales gains [E8, E65, E66].
